ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transaction Reports Act (FTRA), Article 5-2 special measures on confirmation of beneficial owners, as amended, and its Enforcement Decree; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality; Financial Services Commission and Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) regulations and notices on customer identification, customer due diligence, and beneficial-owner verification; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Delegated Regulation for designated persons; FATF Recommendation 24 on beneficial ownership transparency.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Registered Corporation Matters)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry of the competent court with jurisdiction over the registered head office of Yuhan Hoesa in South Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention states: obtain a court-certified copy of the certificate, then obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (MOFA) - do not add consular legalization. Non-Apostille states: obtain the same court-certified copy, then obtain MOFA authentication, and then consular legalization from the diplomatic mission of the destination jurisdiction in Seoul - do not use Apostille. The two paths are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (composite Certificate of Corporate Registration and Tax Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court Registry Office (for corporate registration) and the National Tax Service district tax office (for tax clearance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: after issuance, the document is legalized solely by an MOFA Apostille. For non-Apostille states: after issuance and MOFA authentication, the document is submitted to the destination state's embassy/consulate in Seoul for consular legalization. Never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing incorporation-related matters and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa acting in accordance with the Articles of Association; signatures confirmed by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: This is a private corporate document and must first be notarized by a Korean notary. Thereafter, for Apostille states, only an MOFA Apostille is required. For non-Apostille states, after notarization and MOFA authentication, the destination embassy/consulate in Seoul must consularly legalize the document. The two paths are parallel and never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (certified duplicate of the registered version)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa and the initial incorporators, with the certified duplicate issued by the District Court Registry at which the articles were registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille states: the certified court duplicate is authenticated solely by MOFA Apostille. Non-Apostille states: the certified court duplicate is examined by MOFA and then legalized by the destination state's consulate/embassy in South Korea. Use only the path applicable to the destination jurisdiction; never apply both procedures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by the company's Korean deposit-taking bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A bank duly licensed in South Korea (for example Shinhan Bank, KEB Hana Bank, Woori Bank, or KB Kookmin Bank) at the branch where the Yuhan Hoesa account is held
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter is a private commercial instrument; it must bear the branch manager's seal/signature and, where destination law requires, be notarized. For Apostille states, the notarized letter then receives an MOFA Apostille only. For non-Apostille states, the notarized letter receives MOFA authentication and then consular legalization at the destination mission in Seoul. Do not apply both procedures to one document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and material counterparties must be screened, before and continuously after incorporation, against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's risk indicators, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) blacklist and grey-list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the U.S. Treasury OFAC SDN List, the EU and UK financial sanctions consolidated lists, and persons designated under the Republic of Korea's Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. For each match, the firm must freeze assets, file a Suspicious Transaction Report with KoFIU, and reject the relationship. PEP screening must cover national, foreign, and international prominent public functions plus family members and close associates; enhanced due diligence must verify source of wealth and funds, obtain senior-management approval, and apply heightened transaction monitoring for at least the first year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Chapter VI 'Limited Liability Company', Articles 543 through 593; Article 583 (incorporation registration of a Yuhan Hoesa); Article 601 (effect of incorporation registration); Supreme Court Enforcement Rules on Corporation Registration; Telecommunications Business Act, Article 22 for value-added telecommunication business registration; Framework Act on National Taxes for business registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the district court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, processed through the Korea Court Information Center (I/NET); Supreme Court Registration Bureau for nationwide standards.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company together with authenticated Articles of Incorporation under the Supreme Court Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act; however, the aggregate capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully contributed in cash into a blocked escrow capital deposit account at a licensed Korean bank before the registration filing, and the deposit certificate must be exhibited to

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, electronically via the HomeTax portal at www.hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean Yuhan Hoesa must first complete incorporation under the Korean Commercial Act and obtain a domestic place of business. The LLC representative (or authorized resident tax representative) must then apply through the HomeTax portal or in person at the competent district tax office for a Business Registration (Sa-eop-ja Deung-nok). The application requires the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, lease or ownership proof for the domestic business premises, representative identification/power of attorney, bank account details, and initial capital documents. NTS issues a single 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) that simultaneously operates as the VAT registration number; the applicant is registered as a standard taxable person from the date of business commencement. For a foreign company without a domestic place of business, no domestic VAT registration is required; Korean counterparties self-assess VAT and resolve TIN obligations as a non-resident seller. The Korean LLC is, however, a resident taxpayer and must obtain the BRN within 20 days of business commencement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea has no check-the-box passive entity election comparable to U.S. tax classification. Entity taxation is fixed by statute under the Corporate Tax Act and the Value-Added Tax Act; hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory and not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration exemption threshold in KRW; every supplier of goods or services is required to register before or within 20 days from commencement of business. A simplified taxpayer threshold of KRW 80,000,000 annual taxable supplies exists only for certain unincorporated small businesses; a data-center colocation LLC is a standard taxable VAT registrant.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The electronic tax invoice (ETI) is mandatory for tax invoices issued by registered business operators. Invoices are issued through the NTS HomeTax electronic invoice system, using an NTS-issued digital certificate or a registered tax processing/API connection. The ETI must be transmitted to the NTS without additional third-party certification; there is no state-operated real-time VAT clearance, fiscal stamp, or continuous transaction control anti-fraud stamp in Korea. Late or non-issuance, non-transmission, or falsification of an ETI may result in penalty taxes under the VAT Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, the supply of exported goods and certain exported services/offshore services may be zero-rated. For data-center colocation and bare-metal hosting, zero-rating is available only if the service is contractually provided to a foreign recipient and the place of use or performance is conclusively outside Korea or the supply qualifies as an exported service under the Enforcement Decree. If the server/rack space or hosting service is performed or consumed within Korean territory for a foreign customer, the supply is generally treated as a domestic taxable supply at 10% VAT. The taxpayer must separately document and establish cross-border dispatch/delivery or offshore consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration submitted and cleared through the UNI-PASS single-window system; the export declaration confirmation/validated export clearance certificate for physical export components
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment of equipment or goods out of Korea to the foreign customer (where applicable)
Commercial invoice, packing list and any addenda of sale entered into by the Korean LLC and the foreign buyer

Foreign-exchange receipt evidence in the form of bank-issued confirmation of receipt of convertible foreign currency from the overseas purchaser, together with inward remittance or SWIFT advice matching the exported value
Signed service agreement with the non-resident recipient specifying the service scope, place of performance/use, and governing overseas consumption for data-center colocation/hosting exports
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly audit zero-rated export claims. If the required customs clearance or foreign-exchange receipt documentation is missing, incomplete, or inconsistent, the claimed zero rate is denied and the supply is assessed at 10% VAT, plus penalty tax and daily interest by overdue period. Fraudulent zero-rating based on fabricated export declarations, false invoices, unreported foreign currency receipts, or sham service contracts can trigger criminal penalties, disclosure to prosecutorial authorities, collection of unfunded VAT, and retrospective clawback for all open statutory assessment periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with all reporting executed through licensed foreign exchange banks and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates under a nominally liberalized but closely monitored current account regime. Current account transactions such as service fees, data center leasing receivables, trade payments, and ordinary operating settlements are permitted without prior approval provided that genuine underlying documents exist and the settlement is effected through a domestic licensed foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions, however, are subject to declaration, ex-ante report, or authorization depending on the category. The Korean won is not a fully freely convertible offshore currency; non-residents cannot maintain won-denominated accounts outside the licensed domestic banking system, and offshore KRW activity is heavily constrained. Foreign direct investment into a Korean Yuhan Hoesa requires a foreign investment report through MOEF/KOTRA or a designated domestic bank, followed by the opening of a temporary foreign currency deposit account and capital verification. Profit and dividend remittance is treated as a current account transaction once the relevant withholding tax, audited financial statements, and board approval are filed; however, banks will demand the foreign investment registration certificate and will verify that the funds were sourced from retained earnings or recognized capital surplus. Export proceeds must be repatriated through licensed domestic banks within prescribed collection deadlines, while capital remittances outside the originally declared purpose will be blocked by FEIS reporting. From a treasury standpoint, the KRW is convertible for underlying trade and FDI purposes but not as a free offshore deliverable currency; all material FX activity must flow through domestic banks and must be tagged with valid FEIS purpose codes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, export proceeds from goods and services must be received into a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank account within the statutory collection period, generally 18 months from the date of export declaration, with extension possible only through prescribed MOEF/BOK procedures. There is no mandatory fixed percentage surrender to the won in the current Korean regime; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a permissible foreign currency account or convert to KRW through a licensed FX bank. Nevertheless, any foreign currency not needed for approved foreign-currency working capital should be converted promptly under prudent treasury policy, and every receipt must be supported by the export invoice, service contract, and FEIS declaration referencing the colocation or leasing arrangement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Currency Deposit under FIPA) and Basic Operational WON/FCY Account
Basic Operational WON/FCY Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Basic Operational WON/FCY Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs have minimal viability in South Korea. They are legally barred from opening KRW accounts for domestic corporate entities and from executing foreign exchange declarations under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. An EMI cannot function as the primary operating or treasury bank for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa. Any use of an offshore EMI would be limited to non-KRW auxiliary transactions, always through a licensed domestic Korean bank, and would still be subject to Korean tax, customs, and FX reporting overrides. The only compliant treasury architecture is a tier-1 Korean bank onboarding model.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person physical attendance is generally mandatory for at least one statutory director or the named legal representative when opening a corporate account for a foreign-owned Korean LLC. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted as a standard process by tier-1 Korean banks. Some banks may accept a power-of-attorney if the attorney physically appears and holds a notarized and apostilled POA, a certified copy of board resolutions, and the statutory director participates in a live bank video interview, but this is an exception rather than the rule. The bank will also require original corporate seal certificate (injung certificate), articles of incorporation, business registration certificate, and confirmation of the physical data center operating address before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholder or multi-layer non-resident ownership structure obscuring the ultimate beneficial owner of the Korean LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and certified corporate register, full share register, UBO declaration form, ownership chain diagram to the ultimate natural persons, copies of passports for every UBO holding 25% or more, tax residency certificates for all shareholders, notarized board resolution of the ultimate parent, audited financial statements of the direct and ultimate parent, and a signed undertaking confirming no nominee arrangements or bearer shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection or three-party remittance from a jurisdiction or account unrelated to the declared colocation business, creating suspicion of money-laundering layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements from the remitting entity, signed third-party payment declaration explaining the economic rationale, source of wealth letter, source of funds file to the original wealth generation, commercial contract between the remitter and the Korean LLC, sanctions and PEP screening certificates from an internationally recognized screening provider covering UN/EU/OFAC/Korean designations, and legal entity identifier (LEI) documents where available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business profile inconsistency between high-frequency colocation leasing receipts and the absence of verifiable physical infrastructure, staff, or tenant contracts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed colocation service agreements for each tenant, rack and power allocation schedule, service level agreement schedule, facility lease with utility invoices, Tier-3/4 certification documentation, server and networking equipment invoices, depreciation schedule, payroll records, and a detailed projected cash-flow waterfall showing monthly ACH and SWIFT incoming receipts against operating expenditures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder funding or shareholder loan is disproportionate to the company's stated capital and operating scale, creating an unexplained equity risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: MOEF/KOTRA foreign investment report, FEIS declaration number, licensed FX bank capital verification certificate, board resolution authorizing the capital increase or shareholder loan, investor audited financial statements and solvency evidence, Korean tax clearance certificate, the executed shareholder loan agreement with approved interest rate, and an independent valuation of the colocation equipment or facility if the loan is linked to asset acquisition.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor must file the foreign investment report with KOTRA/MOEF or a designated foreign exchange bank prior to remittance. After approval, the investor or the Korean LLC opens a temporary foreign currency deposit account at a tier-1 Korean bank and receives the capital via SWIFT MT103, clearly identifying the investor name, investor registration number, transaction purpose, and FEIS purpose code for direct investment equity subscription. Upon receipt, the bank releases the foreign exchange declaration into FEIS, the LLC completes the foreign investment company registration, and the bank issues a capital verification certificate confirming the paid-in capital. Only then may the full amount be converted to KRW and transferred to the operational account. No part of the capital injection may be commingled with operating revenue, and any deviation from the declared purpose requires a post-change report to the MOEF.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements must be executed through the licensed Korean bank using SWIFT MT103 for services, colocation lease payments, licensing fees, and supplier settlements, always with the underlying contract, tax invoice, and FEIS purpose code. Imported server hardware and data center equipment may be settled through Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700 with reimbursement via MT103/MT202) or Documentary Collections (DP/DA using SWIFT MT400/MT410) when the bank relationship and LC terms support it. Dividend, royalty, and interest remittances require board approval, withholding tax payment proof, audited financials, and FEIS capital transaction filings.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards with a documented underlying colocation, trade, or service transaction, executed only with licensed onshore Korean banks and limited to genuine exposure amounts.

Korean won non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where permitted by MOEF/BOK position limits and executed via a licensed onshore bank against a proven real trade or capital transaction exposure, never on a naked speculative basis.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps permitted for eligible underlying capital transactions such as foreign currency shareholder loans or equipment financing, subject to FEIS reporting, board approval, and bank credit/ISDA documentation.
FX options with real-demand underlying exposure, used as hedging instruments only, with premiums and notional amounts tied to the actual colocation or trade contract.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, including the Corporate Tax Base Statement and Tax Reconciliation Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea via the Hometax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing deadline is March 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or understating taxable income triggers delinquency penalties of up to 20% of the unpaid tax for unfiled returns, 10% to 20% for underreported income, plus daily late-payment interest of 0.022% on arrears. Prolonged non-filing leads to forced collection, seizure of bank accounts, and administrative cancellation of the business registration, although South Korea does not apply an automatic commercial-register strike-off for tax filings alone.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Tax Authority of the relevant Si/Gun/Gu (city, county, or district) through the Wetax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing and payment deadline is April 30 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and nonpayment attract local-income-tax additional levies of 20% for unfiled returns, 10% for underreported local income tax, and daily interest of 0.022%. Persistent noncompliance results in administrative collection, property attachment, and cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Advance Returns for the January-March and July-September preliminary systems
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea via Hometax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January-March advance VAT return due April 30; July-September advance VAT return due October 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted VAT advance filings expose the company to a 10% negligence penalty on the unreported tax amount, 20% for flagrant underreporting, daily 0.022% arrears interest, and enhanced collection enforcement including seizure of receivables and bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Final Returns for the January-June and July-December taxable periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea via Hometax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year final return due July 25; second half-year final return due January 25 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of the final VAT return triggers a 10% non-filing penalty and 20% penalty for intentional underreporting, together with daily arrears interest of 0.022%. Continued noncompliance leads to tax authority administrative revocation of the business registration and forced collection against corporate assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer Annual Wage and Salary Withholding Reconciliation Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea via Hometax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 10 of the calendar year following the year of withholding
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual withholding reconciliation triggers additional withholding taxes of 20% of the understated tax plus daily arrears interest of 0.022%. For payroll compliance, the responsible controlling officer may also be subject to monetary sanctions, and persistent failure can trigger tax authority enforcement and business registration cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary Annual Members' Meeting of the Yuhan Hoesa for approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records only; no external filing to a company registry is required unless a registered matter changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the meeting must be held no later than June 30 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual members' meeting may expose responsible managing officers to administrative fines under the Korean Commercial Act and to civil liability for false financial statements. It cannot by itself produce a corporate strike-off, but it undermines the company's ability to satisfy tax and audit deadlines and supports creditor liquidation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Auditor Report and Audited Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service of South Korea (FSS) and the Financial Services Commission for mandatory-audit corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For mandatory-audit companies, no later than four months after fiscal year-end and prior to the annual members' meeting; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, this effectively requires filing by April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the company fails to appoint an external auditor or submit the audit report, the Financial Services Commission may designate an auditor and impose administrative fines up to KRW 30 million. The auditor designation costs are borne by the company, and continued noncompliance can trigger regulatory enforcement, restriction of credit reporting, and disqualification of officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Related Change Report and Member Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy reporting channel or designated foreign exchange bank, as applicable; court registry for registered-entity matters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any transfer of a membership interest or any change in foreign investor status, shareholder identity, contribution structure, or foreign ownership ratio
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the foreign-investment change report within 30 days may result in administrative fines, loss of foreign-investment protections, and penalty interest on tax benefits received. Delayed court registration of changes to registered company matters may trigger negligence penalties under the Commercial Act and may render such changes unenforceable against third parties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily subject to an independent certified public accountant audit if, at the fiscal year-end, it meets any of the following quantitative balance sheet, turnover, or headcount triggers: (i) it is a listed or publicly issued company; (ii) it is a financial company or is otherwise statutorily designated as requiring an audit; (iii) its total assets are at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million); (iv) its total assets are at least KRW 8 billion (approximately USD 6.1 million) and either its annual revenue is at least KRW 40 billion (approximately USD 30.7 million) or its average full-time regular employees number 300 or more; or (v) it is specifically designated by the Financial Services Commission for a statutory external audit. Below these thresholds, an ordinary non-listed small- or medium-sized Yuhan Hoesa is not required to obtain a statutory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for publicly accountable companies and mandatory-audit listed entities; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for non-public and small- to medium-sized companies, including Yuhan Hoesa; tax-basis accounting schedules prepared under the Korean Corporate Tax Law are required for filing purposes. Audit-exempt small companies may maintain simplified internal books, but if an audit is mandatory, the audited statements must be prepared in accordance with K-IFRS or K-GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a general annual UBO confirmation filing for an ordinary non-listed Yuhan Hoesa. However, the company is required to keep an up-to-date register of members at all times, and any transfer of a membership interest must be recorded in the members' register and, if the transferor or transferee is a foreign investor, reported under the

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% top marginal corporate income tax rate (progressive brackets: 9% on the first KRW 200 million; 19% on the next KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on taxable income above KRW 20 billion), plus a 10% local income tax surtax on the national corporate tax, yielding an aggregate top statutory rate of approximately 23.1% before treaty limitations
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying foreign-invested and high-technology businesses operating in Foreign Exclusive Zones and Free Economic Zones may enjoy statutory tax holidays including a 100% corporate tax exemption for the first five years and a 50% reduction for the following two years. Additional applicable incentives include R&D tax credits for data center software and energy-efficiency upgrades, job creation credits, facility investment credits for strategic national technologies, and deductibility for qualifying technology acquisition costs. Korea also applies a substance-based preferential rule for foreign direct investment in designated advanced industries; however, pure passive leasing of server rack space generally requires a tax ruling to secure zone-based incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Return (National Tax Service Form 4-1) filed through the HomeTax electronic portal (Hometax), together with required attachments including the financial statements, tax adjustment schedules, audit report, and supplementary transfer pricing and foreign ownership schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months from the end of each fiscal year: a December 31 fiscal year-end requires filing by March 31 of the following calendar year. A non-resident-invested company may apply for an extension of up to one month (or longer in exceptional cases) by filing a permission request, but the extension does not defer payment of provisional and withholding tax obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business Registration Number and statutory corporate identification data of the Yuhan Hoesa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the 10-digit registration number assigned by the National Tax Service. This field only identifies the Korean taxpayer and does not list non-resident shareholders; foreign shareholding is reported separately in the foreign investor ledger and the withholding declaration annex. Ensure the representative director and address are current because NTS correspondence relating to non-resident tax assessments will be mailed to this address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year or tax return period in the format YYYY.MM.DD to YYYY.MM.DD
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean Yuhan Hoesa normally follows the calendar year. If the overseas parent uses a different accounting period and a special fiscal year has been approved by the NTS, use that approved period and attach the approval notice. Mismatched fiscal periods between the Korean entity and the foreign beneficial owner may delay DTA relief applications and should be reconciled in the transfer pricing master file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue, including data center colocation fees, bare-metal server leasing revenue, rack space leases, bandwidth charges, power distribution charges, cooling service fees, maintenance contracts and any other operating income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue in Korean won on an accrual basis. Foreign-currency receipts received via Swift wire or monthly ACH from overseas customers must be converted at the exchange rate prescribed by the Tax Act. Do not net colocation revenue against cross-charges paid to a foreign data-center operator or parent entity; all gross receipts are taxable Korean-source income unless an explicit treaty or domestic rule recharacterizes the activity. Under-reporting of overseas bare-metal hosting income is the most common non-resident audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, including cost of sales, depreciation of servers and cooling equipment, electricity charges, bandwidth costs, personnel costs, rent, maintenance, interest, taxes other than corporate income tax, and bad debts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach itemized tax-adjustment schedules. Expenses paid or accrued to non-resident affiliates, such as management fees, technical service fees, intra-group interest, and cloud licensing royalties, are deductible only if the transactions are at arm's length, supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, and, where domestic law requires, withholding tax has been properly withheld. Payments to a foreign related lender may be partially non-deductible under Korea's thin-capitalization rule; the disallowed interest must be added back in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base before loss carry-forward deduction, being the adjusted income after applying statutory loss deductions and non-taxable items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile this amount with the audited Korean financial statements. Any transfer pricing adjustment from Korean-source revenue shifted to an overseas affiliate must be added back. Non-resident ownership does not reduce this figure; Korean corporate tax is computed on the entire income of the domestic legal entity, not on a remittance basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss carry-forward deduction applied within the statutory carryforward period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct allowable losses carried forward from the preceding ten taxable years, filed with a loss carry-forward ledger. Losses attributable to a foreign branch or foreign permanent establishment may not be offset against Korean domestic-source income except where permitted by the Korean tax law. If there has been a substantial change in ownership or the business was terminated, the NTS may deny the deduction under anti-abuse rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after the loss carry-forward deduction, the amount to which corporate tax rates are applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If this amount is zero, enter zero and attach supporting loss documentation. For a non-resident-owned data center company claiming a Free Economic Zone exemption, compute the taxable amount before applying the exemption and identify the exempt slice in the attached schedule; a failure to show the computation may expose the exemption to reversal on audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax, local income tax surtax, and any tax reductions related to foreign investment, free economic zone status, or technology promotion incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the progressive rates: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 21% on Korean taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion. Add local income tax at 10% of the national corporate tax. For qualifying foreign-invested enterprises, subtract the tax holiday amount and attach the investment approval and tax exemption ruling. Treaty provisions do not reduce corporate income tax; they only affect withholding taxes on outbound distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and deductions including foreign tax credits, R&D credits, job creation credits, facility investment credits, disaster loss credits, and interim taxes paid
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available only for foreign-source income and must be computed using the aggregate limitation method. Non-resident shareholders cannot claim a Korean foreign tax credit on their own behalf in this return. Attach the relevant credit schedules and, if any remittance of interest, royalty or dividend withholding tax has already been made, record the creditable withholding amount to avoid double-counting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable after deduction of declared provisional tax payments, withholding credits, and advance payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The final balance must be paid when the return is filed. If the company has distributed dividends to a non-resident corporate or individual shareholder, the withholding tax on such dividends is not paid in this box; it is reported in the separate withholding tax return, and the Yuhan Hoesa is the withholding agent. Any undisclosed dividend distribution with a missing withholding return triggers an immediate 22% withholding claim and criminal referral risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attachments: audited financial statements, tax adjustment calculation annexes, consolidated group schedules, foreign shareholder register, transfer pricing documentation summary, and tax treaty relief applications
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the auditor's report if total assets exceed the statutory external audit threshold. Attach the foreign shareholder ledger showing the name, country, tax residence, ownership percentage, and ultimate beneficial owner of each non-resident investor. If treaty relief was applied to dividends, interest, or royalties during the year, attach the approved application forms, the Tax Residency Certificates, and the beneficial ownership substantiation; non-approval must be disclosed as a contingency.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file a corporate tax return by the deadline triggers a non-reporting negligence tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; unfaithful under-reporting triggers a 10% penalty on the understated taxable amount, and fraudulent under-reporting triggers a 30% penalty. In addition, a late-payment surcharge accrues at 0.0225% per day for each day the tax remains unpaid, subject to statutory caps. Failure to attach transfer pricing documentation may draw an additional administrative penalty and the corporate tax return may be treated as noncompliant for advance-pricing agreement purposes. Criminal thresholds are crossed where false returns are prepared with intent to evade tax; tax evasion exceeding KRW 300 million is prosecutable as aggravated tax crime and can result in imprisonment for a term of between three and ten years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on gross dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax; where a bilateral Double Tax Agreement applies, the rate may be reduced to 15%, 10%, or 5% depending on the treaty and the shareholder's ownership percentage and substance
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the paying Korean Yuhan Hoesa must, before or at the time of remittance, collect an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the non-resident recipient's residence State, verified proof that the recipient is the beneficial owner, and evidence of the business or equity relationship supporting the ownership threshold. The withholding agent submits the official treaty-relief application to the competent Korean tax office, usually with the withholding tax return, and must disclose the ultimate beneficial owner and lack of any conduit arrangement. If the application is rejected, the full statutory 22% must be withheld and paid; the non-resident may apply for a refund through a domestic claim within the applicable statutory period. A TRC older than the payment date, a certificate lacking signature, or an unexplained nominee shareholder creates immediate denial risk and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding rates are 22% (20% plus 2% local surtax) for interest and royalties paid to non-residents. Under most Korean bilateral tax treaties, interest may be reduced to 10% and royalties to 10-15%, while dividends are reduced to 15% (with a 10% or 5% rate for substantial shareholdings depending on the DTA). Payment of intercompany debt interest to a foreign parent shareholder may also be restricted by the Korean thin-capitalization rule and by treaty non-discrimination considerations; royalty payments to a non-resident recipient without a Korean permanent establishment must satisfy transfer pricing and registered technology-contract filing duties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File and simplified documentation are mandatory for Korean entities whose gross revenue for the fiscal year exceeds KRW 100 billion or whose cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion; a consolidated group with revenue of at least KRW 100 billion must prepare a Master File, and a Country-by-Country Report is required where the multinational group's consolidated revenue equals or exceeds KRW 1 trillion. These thresholds are reviewed annually by the National Tax Service and should be monitored on a real-time basis for a data center colocation entity due to the high volume of international recharges and equipment lease transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies the substance-over-form principle under Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 2-5 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. Although Korea has not enacted UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, the National Tax Service consistently applies the OECD Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) analysis when determining whether a Korean subsidiary involved in data-center colocation has actual personnel, decision-making functions, operational control, asset management, and risk assumption. A Yuhan Hoesa that merely holds invoices, routes dividends, or invoices rack-space fees without local technical staff, network monitoring, physical security oversight, and independent contract negotiation will fail the substance doctrine and may be denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fictitious Cost Inflation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company deliberately invoices only a portion of the data center colocation and bare-metal hosting fees, records customer payments received by foreign agents as loans, or inflates maintenance and power costs paid to a related non-resident entity, thereby understating Korean taxable income and evading corporate income tax. This conduct typically appears as unexplained cash deposits, ACH churn to overseas accounts, and unrecorded Swift wire revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A 20% to 30% negligence tax surcharge on the understated tax amount under Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus late-payment daily interest charges. Criminal prosecution under Article 10 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act and Article 13 of the Act on Aggravated Punishment for Specific Crimes applies where the evaded tax exceeds statutory thresholds, carrying imprisonment of up to ten years and fines of up to five times the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the corporate form is used as a sham to evade taxes, a court may pierce the corporate veil and hold the representative director and managing directors jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and interest. Directors who directly prepared false books may be personally blacklisted by the National Tax Service, subject to a travel ban, have assets attached, and be sentenced to criminal imprisonment. The companies law also permits civil creditors and minority shareholders to sue directors for compensatory damages arising from intentional or negligent compliance failures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Arm's Length Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity charges an offshore data-center affiliate below-arm's-length rack lease and cooling-service rates, or pays substantially inflated management, software, and coordination fees to the foreign parent, transferring profit outside Korea without any functional compensation, personnel, or capital contribution; simultaneously, the statutory Master File, Local File, or Country-by-Country Report is not prepared, attached, or contemporaneously updated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service is entitled to adjust taxable income to the arm's length result under Article 5 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs and impose an additional 20% to 30% unfaithful-reporting negligence tax on the adjusted under-reported income. Failure to submit transfer pricing documentation triggers separate administrative penalties, and the NTS may apply penalties of up to 100% of the tax difference in aggravated non-compliance situations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or execute the false intercompany pricing scheme are jointly liable for restitution of the tax gain when the company is unable to pay after the adjustment. In egregious cases, a court may disregard the limited liability of the Yuhan Hoesa and hold the directors personally liable for the entire adjusted tax, penalties, and interest. Travel restrictions, asset seizures, and civil damages actions are routinely combined with criminal charges for violation of the International Tax Adjustment Act and fraud under the Korean Criminal Act, leading to imprisonment terms of up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Shopping, Shell Ownership and False Beneficial Owner Representation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean operating company is owned through a tax-haven or intermediate holding company with no office, employee, or substantive business activity; the intermediate company claims an improper reduced DTA withholding rate on dividends, interest, or royalties sourced from Korea, while the ultimate beneficial owner remains a Korean resident or a resident of a jurisdiction with no favorable treaty. The Yuhan Hoesa files treaty relief applications using false certificate declarations and does not disclose the ultimate beneficiary, or it uses professional service agreements to disguise equity dividends as deductible royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will deny treaty benefits under Article 2-5 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs and the domestic General Anti-Avoidance Rule. The company must pay the full statutory 22% withholding tax on all distributions, together with a 20% negligence penalty for non-withholding, daily overdue charges, and interest. Submitting false beneficial ownership declarations constitutes tax fraud and deception, which triggers criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, including imprisonment up to three years or fines up to five times the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced where the Korean entity is operated as a conduit with no genuine business purpose. Each director who signed or knowingly facilitated the false treaty application is personally liable for the un-withheld tax and penalties if the company becomes insolvent. The NTS will impose individual blacklisting and a travel ban for responsible directors, and the courts may enter personal civil restitution judgments for the full amount of tax advantage obtained. Criminal conviction can lead to imprisonment, disqualification from serving as a director in Korea, and deportation if the director is a non-resident.
